findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the standard library's `proxy_bypass_environment` and httpx 0.28's `NO_PROXY` mount patterns differ (leading dot, scheme-qualified entries). Either list each difference as a deliberate one or drop the 'httpx's own default' equivalence, and add a test for the leading-dot case.
evidence: Plan: "with standard-library semantics: httpx's own default, with 3 deliberate differences below"

Not established anywhere: the plan does not show that `urllib.request.proxy_bypass` and httpx's `get_environment_proxies` mount patterns treat `NO_PROXY` the same way. httpx's source is in site-packages, which the repo tools cannot read, so the plan's claim is unverified.
findings.finding: The plan presents the routing as 'standard-library semantics: httpx's own default, with 3 deliberate differences below', which treats the two as identical apart from those three points. It cites no comparison of how they parse `NO_PROXY`, and they likely differ. httpx 0.28 turns each `NO_PROXY` entry into a mount pattern: `.example.com` becomes `*.example.com` (subdomains only), and scheme-qualified entries such as `http://host` are honoured. The standard library's `proxy_bypass_environment` strips a leading dot, matches both the bare domain and its subdomains, and does not understand scheme-qualified entries. Any such difference is a fourth, undeclared one.
findings.location: Approach, first paragraph ('standard-library semantics: httpx's own default, with 3 deliberate differences')
scenarios: `NO_PROXY=.corp.example` with a gateway at `corp.example`: the standard library bypasses the proxy, while httpx's default would proxy it.
`NO_PROXY=http://internal-llm`: httpx's default would bypass the proxy for that scheme and host; the standard-library matcher would not.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either list NO_PROXY matching (urllib proxy_bypass_environment vs httpx's URL-pattern mounts, e.g. scheme-qualified `http://host` entries) as a 4th deliberate difference, or reproduce httpx's NO_PROXY semantics; add a test for the chosen behaviour on a URL-form NO_PROXY entry.
evidence: Plan: "with standard-library semantics: httpx's own default, with 3 deliberate differences below" and "a host matched by `NO_PROXY` (`urllib.request.proxy_bypass` ...) goes direct".
Web: httpx's environment-variable docs give `NO_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1,python-httpx.org` as a valid example and say these requests bypass the proxy.
Web: httpx turns NO_PROXY hostnames into mount patterns (`mounts[f"all://*{hostname}"] = None`) (encode/httpx #1536). That is a different matcher from urllib's suffix matching.
The test list covers only a simple matched host and an unmatched host, not URL-form or IPv6 NO_PROXY entries.
findings.finding: The plan says its behaviour is "httpx's own default, with 3 deliberate differences". But it matches NO_PROXY with `urllib.request.proxy_bypass`, which is the standard library's matcher, not httpx's. httpx turns NO_PROXY entries into its own URL patterns and documents URL-form entries such as `http://127.0.0.1`. urllib's proxy_bypass_environment only does hostname/suffix comparisons, so a scheme-qualified entry never matches. This is a 4th, undocumented difference. The plan does not verify it or tell users about it, and no test covers it.
findings.location: Approach ("standard-library semantics: httpx's own default, with 3 deliberate differences") / Implementation per-request bullet / Tests
scenarios: A user whose NO_PROXY was written for httpx contains `https://llm.internal.example` (URL form, as httpx documents). rebar's OpenAI-compatible client then sends that request through the corporate proxy, which may refuse it, so the gate returns INDETERMINATE.
Someone reading the plan or docstring assumes rebar behaves exactly like httpx apart from the 3 listed points and misdiagnoses a routing difference.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the Approach sentence to: "proxy selection follows httpx's default; NO_PROXY matching follows the standard library (`urllib.request.proxy_bypass_environment`), which, unlike httpx, ignores scheme-qualified entries such as `http://host`." findings.finding: The plan says a proxy refusal (httpx.ProxyError) is deliberately not retried, but it does not say how that failure reaches the operator. The Anthropic SDK wraps any non-timeout httpx exception as APIConnectionError, and pydantic-ai turns that into ModelAPIError. failure.py `_map` sends a bare ModelAPIError to RETRY_NOW ('Transient connection blip — retry immediately.', exit 11). So after the fix, a sandbox proxy that refuses the host (for example, api.anthropic.com not on the allowlist, CONNECT 403) will still be reported as a transient blip and the operator told to retry. That is the same mislabelling the problem statement describes, and it contradicts the plan's own 'not retried' decision.
findings.location: Approach > Implementation > 'Failure disposition' bullet; src/rebar/llm/failure.py::_map (lines 285-309)
scenarios: In the Claude Code sandbox, api.anthropic.com is not on the allowlist. The proxy returns 403 to CONNECT, httpx raises ProxyError, and the gate reports 'Transient connection blip — retry immediately' with exit 11, so callers keep retrying.

findings.finding: The proxy-refusal arm has no stated caller-facing disposition. The plan says `httpx.ProxyError` 'is not retried', which covers only the transport layer. The SDK wraps transport exceptions, so the error would likely surface as APIConnectionError → ModelAPIError('Connection error.'), fail over across FallbackModel candidates, and be classified as 'Transient connection blip' / INDETERMINATE. That label is the same misleading one the Context section records. A proxy 403/407 (for example, the sandbox denying a host not on its allowlist) is a permanent or config failure, yet the plan never says whether `classify_llm_failure` should surface it as retryable or fatal.

scenarios: Claude Code sandbox where api.anthropic.com is not on the allowlist: the proxy returns 403 on CONNECT, ProxyError surfaces as 'Connection error.', and the operator sees INDETERMINATE 'Transient connection blip' and retries forever.

findings.finding: The plan says the variables are read once at construction ("reads the variables once at construction with `urllib.request.getproxies_environment()`"). But the per-request NO_PROXY check calls `urllib.request.proxy_bypass(host)`. That function calls getproxies_environment() again on every call: on macOS and Windows it reads the environment to choose between the environment matcher and the system-config matcher, and on Linux proxy_bypass_environment reads `no_proxy` from os.environ when no dict is passed. So NO_PROXY is read per request, not at construction, and the routing decision can mix construction-time proxy values with request-time NO_PROXY values. The claim that "[the] environment matcher applies whenever proxy variables are set" also depends on what the environment holds at request time, not on the transport's stored dict.
findings.location: Approach / Implementation — `_env_proxy_aware_transport` bullet and per-request bullet
scenarios: A long-lived process, or a test's monkeypatch.delenv, removes the proxy variables after the client is built. On macOS, proxy_bypass then falls back to `proxy_bypass_macosx_sysconf`, so system-proxy exceptions decide routing even though the plan says the system proxy is never consulted (difference #1).
A test changes NO_PROXY after building the client and sees routing change, which contradicts the read-once design.
findings.suggested_fix: In the per-request bullet, replace `urllib.request.proxy_bypass(host)` with `urllib.request.proxy_bypass_environment(host, self._proxies)`. This uses the stored `no` entry, never dispatches to the macOS/Windows system-config matcher, and makes NO_PROXY read once together with the proxy variables.

evidence: 'Loopback hosts (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`, `0.0.0.0`, `*.localhost`; rebar's existing `_LOOPBACK_HOSTS` set)'
findings.finding: The loopback list includes `*.localhost` and calls it 'rebar's existing `_LOOPBACK_HOSTS` set'. A set of exact hostnames cannot match a wildcard, so the plan leaves open whether a suffix check must be added and whether the whole 127.0.0.0/8 range counts.
findings.location: Implementation, deliberate difference 2
scenarios: A host such as `ollama.localhost` or `127.0.0.2` is sent to the proxy
findings.suggested_fix: Define `_is_loopback_host(h) = h.lower() in _LOOPBACK_HOSTS or h.lower().endswith('.localhost')` without modifying `_LOOPBACK_HOSTS`, and state the default for the 127/8 range (e.g. use `ipaddress.ip_address(h).is_loopback` when h is an IP).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the disposition when the post-skip fallback leg (next proxy or direct) fails, and ensure the surfaced failure names the skipped unusable proxy variable rather than only a transient connection blip.
evidence: "is skipped with a WARNING that names the variable but never its value ... The request falls back to the next applicable proxy or goes direct, as it did before, instead of every LLM call failing at construction."
No statement of what the caller sees when the direct or next-proxy leg then fails.
findings.finding: The skip-unusable-proxy fallback arm has no stated fallback-failure disposition. When a proxy value is unusable (for example SOCKS without socksio), the plan falls back to the next proxy or goes direct, and only logs a WARNING. On a proxy-only-egress host, the direct leg then fails with gaierror → ConnectError, which is a retryable NetworkError classified as a transient blip. The permanent root cause (an unusable proxy configuration) is masked by the fallback leg's 'transient' failure. The plan does not say which disposition wins when the fallback itself fails.
findings.location: Approach > Implementation > 'Deliberate differences' item 3
scenarios: Sandbox exporting ALL_PROXY=socks5://... with socksio not installed: the skip goes direct, gaierror is retried, the review returns INDETERMINATE 'Transient connection blip', and the only clue is a WARNING in a log.
findings.suggested_fix: When any proxy variable was skipped as unusable and the fallback leg then fails to connect, include the skipped variable's name in the surfaced failure reason, and classify the failure as a configuration error rather than a transient blip.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge hosts that have proxy variables set and currently connect directly; document NO_PROXY as the opt-out in the change notes or docs.
evidence: "No `http`/`https`/`all` proxy set: it returns `http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport()`, the exact object built before, so behaviour is unchanged."
"No new config key, env var or flag."
No mention of hosts with proxy variables set that currently succeed directly.
findings.finding: The plan changes behaviour for existing hosts that already have HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY/ALL_PROXY set but whose direct egress to the LLM endpoint works today. Those LLM calls will now be routed through the proxy. Examples are corporate CI runners and developer workstations with a proxy exported for other tools, or a proxy that blocks or does not allow-list the LLM host. The plan only asserts 'unchanged' for the no-variable case. It does not acknowledge this population or name NO_PROXY as their documented opt-out, for instance in a changelog or docs note.
findings.location: Approach (first paragraph) and Acceptance Criteria bullet 2
scenarios: A CI runner exports HTTPS_PROXY for package mirrors, but the proxy does not allow api.anthropic.com. Gate calls that succeeded directly yesterday now fail via ProxyError.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Approach and a changelog or docs entry: 'Hosts with HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY set will now route LLM calls through that proxy (matching curl, the anthropic SDK and boto3); add the LLM host to NO_PROXY to keep direct connections.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Isolate existing transport-seam tests from ambient *_PROXY variables (shared or conftest proxy-env scrub, or explicit monkeypatch.delenv) and verify their fakes tolerate a `proxy=` keyword.
evidence: "A `clean_proxy_env` fixture removes every `*_proxy` variable first" — defined for the new test_llm_env_proxy.py only
"keeping the tests' monkeypatch seam" implies existing tests patch AsyncHTTPTransport
AC: "`make verify` passes on the change" together with the in-sandbox run, where HTTPS_PROXY is set
findings.finding: Existing tests that monkeypatch `http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport` (the seam the plan relies on) become ambient-environment-dependent. The `clean_proxy_env` fixture is scoped to the new test module only. When `make verify` runs with HTTPS_PROXY set — as it would inside the sandbox named in the acceptance criteria — existing fakes will see `proxy=` calls. If those fakes do not accept a `proxy` keyword, the error could be swallowed by the 'unusable proxy → skip' path, or existing tests could get `_EnvProxyRoutingTransport` instead of the plain transport they assert on. The plan schedules no modify-test or isolation work for the existing provider tests.
findings.location: Tests section; 'Transports are built via http_module.AsyncHTTPTransport looked up at call time, keeping the tests' monkeypatch seam.'
scenarios: A developer or agent runs `make verify` inside the Claude Code sandbox, where HTTPS_PROXY is exported. Existing anthropic_model/providers tests now take the routing path and fail or warn, so the outcome depends on the host environment.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an 'Alternatives considered' note comparing `_EnvProxyRoutingTransport` with httpx's `mounts=` (per-mount retry wrapping, built from the same environment variables), and record why the custom router wins (httpx2 parity, NO_PROXY matching semantics, a single retry layer).
evidence: Plan: "It implements the async transport protocol itself (no subclass), so one class serves httpx and httpx2." `mounts=` appears nowhere in the plan.
Web: httpx maintainers' answer to the same question is to configure `mounts={"https://": httpx.HTTPTransport(proxy=...), "http://": httpx.HTTPTransport()}` (encode/httpx discussion #1635).

Web: another project with the same problem fixed it by mounting "one proxy transport per scheme from the environment, and a direct route for each NO_PROXY entry" (entropy-data-sdk-python PR #1). A third project explicitly rejected mounts because of private URLPattern semantics (StayPirate/sentinel #998). Either way, comparing the two is standard practice.
findings.finding: The plan builds a new routing transport class (_EnvProxyRoutingTransport) without considering httpx's built-in way to route requests to different transports: the client's `mounts=` URL-pattern map. httpx itself uses mounts to apply the environment proxies. The plan never names it or says why it was rejected. The plan's stated reasons (one class for both httpx and httpx2, and retry wrapping above the routing) may justify the choice, but they are not compared with the alternative: per-mount retry wrapping, e.g. `AsyncClient(transport=retry(direct), mounts={'https://': retry(AsyncHTTPTransport(proxy=...)), 'all://*nohost': ...})`.
findings.location: Approach / Implementation — `_EnvProxyRoutingTransport` bullet
scenarios: A maintainer later wonders why rebar has its own routing class rather than httpx mounts, and either rewrites it or copies the pattern to new clients with no recorded reasoning.

httpx or httpx2 changes the async transport protocol (for example new lifecycle hooks). A protocol-only class that does not subclass the base may stop matching silently, while mounts would keep working.
findings.suggested_fix: Under Approach, add a short 'Alternatives considered' paragraph. It should say that httpx's own environment-proxy support is `mounts` built by `httpx._utils.get_environment_proxies()`, which is private and also reads the macOS/Windows system proxy. It should explain that rebuilding mounts by hand would need a retry wrapper for each mount, plus httpx's URLPattern semantics for NO_PROXY, on both httpx and httpx2. That is why a single protocol-level router under one retry wrapper was chosen.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that the real `httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport` accepts `proxy=`, and add one test that builds `_env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2)` without the recording factory while HTTPS_PROXY is set, so it would fail on a signature mismatch.
evidence: Partially-verified: `httpx2` and `httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport` resolve in the venv (resolve_symbol EXISTS), but the `proxy=` keyword on httpx2's constructor was not observed. The plan's only evidence about the proxy keyword concerns httpx 0.28.1.

Plan: 'A recording factory replaces `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport` (the existing seam) and records each transport's `proxy=`'. A stand-in factory cannot detect a signature mismatch in the real httpx2 class.
Plan, difference 3: only an unknown scheme or SOCKS without socksio is treated as an unusable value to skip. A constructor TypeError is not covered.
findings.finding: `httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport` accepting the `proxy=` keyword is assumed but never verified. The plan's evidence is entirely about httpx (`httpx 0.28.1 sets allow_env_proxies...`, the experiment with `httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(proxy=...)`). The 'httpx2 wrapper routing' test uses a recording factory in place of AsyncHTTPTransport, and that factory accepts any keyword argument. If the real httpx2 constructor names the keyword differently or rejects it, it raises TypeError. TypeError is not one of the exceptions the 'unusable proxy value is skipped' rule catches (ValueError/ImportError), so on the httpx2 path every LLM client would fail at construction whenever a proxy variable is set.
findings.location: Approach > Implementation ('one class serves httpx and httpx2'; 'AsyncHTTPTransport(proxy=<url>) per distinct proxy URL'); Tests ('httpx2 wrapper routing')
scenarios: The installed anthropic SDK annotates `http_client` as `httpx2.AsyncClient`, so `_anthropic_http_client_module` returns httpx2. With HTTPS_PROXY set, `_EnvProxyRoutingTransport` calls `httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport(proxy=url)`. If that keyword doesn't exist, every gate LLM call fails at construction, which is worse than today's INDETERMINATE.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test case that sets HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:9 and calls `_env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2)` with no monkeypatched factory. Assert it returns `_EnvProxyRoutingTransport` and that the proxied inner transport was built. Do the same for httpx. Record the observed httpx2 constructor signature in the plan's Root cause section.
